- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp sentiment spikes (≥0.67 with +0.33+ sentiment change), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–4% for 1–5 day horizons.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.33+ change) and news volume is high; add 0.5–2% to forecast for 1–3 day horizons.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in sentiment + price, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true prices.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and news volume is low; reduce forecast by 1–3% to match true mean.
